title: Whom do you seek? (John 18:1–11)
hookLine: soldiers with torches; he steps forward: I am he, and they fall back

lines: ACROSS THE KIDRON, INTO A GARDEN.
cards: The prayer is over. They walk out into the dark, across the brook Kidron, into a garden. John says Judas knew the place, because Jesus often went there with his friends.

And Judas comes, with a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, carrying lanterns, torches and weapons. A quiet garden at night, and suddenly a line of firelight moving through it.
Jesus doesn't wait to be found.

teach.h: HE STEPS FORWARD: WHOM SEEK YE?
teach.b: John tells it this way, in the King James Bible: Jesus, "knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye?"

teach.h: I AM HE, AND THEY FALL BACK.
teach.b: They answer, Jesus of Nazareth. He says two words: I am he. Then something strange: "As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground."
Why would armed men fall over? Look at the Greek.
He says ego eimi, I am. The he is added in English; many printings of the King James put it in italics to show it isn't in the Greek. All through John, I am has done heavy lifting.
I am the bread of life. I am the light of the world. Before Abraham was, I am.
Some readers hear an echo of God's name given to Moses at the burning bush, I AM. So when the soldiers stagger back, John seems to show who is really in charge in this garden.
Then Jesus asks again, and bargains, not for himself but for his friends: if you're looking for me, let these go. Peter has other ideas.
He pulls a sword and cuts off the right ear of the high priest's servant. Only John gives the servant's name: Malchus.
And Jesus says: "Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?" No fighting. He walks into it with his eyes open.

how: Many churches read John's account of the arrest during Holy Week, and on Good Friday in a number of traditions the whole Passion according to John is read or sung aloud, often with different readers taking the parts.

games.q: you're in a dark garden. soldiers with torches are coming for you. your friends are frozen. what do you do?
o: step forward and ask: whom seek ye?
games.why: he goes out to meet them, says 'I am he', and asks them to let his friends go.

practice: Think of something hard coming toward you, a dreaded conversation, a bill, a diagnosis, an apology you owe, and notice the urge to hide in the trees until it finds you.
Picture yourself stepping forward first, calm, saying in your own way, here I am. If you pray, ask for that kind of courage; if not, simply rehearse the first step.
